The AI-Ready Website.

A better-looking website that works harder for your business and gets found by AI search.

AI is changing how people find businesses. More of your customers are asking ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini instead of scrolling search results. The good news: the same tools make it faster and more affordable than ever to bring your website up to date.

Why now

How people search has changed

AI tools answer questions directly, often without a click. If your site isn’t structured for them, your business gets left out of the answer.

Updating your site got easier

AI helps us review, restructure and rewrite faster, so a real upgrade no longer means a long, expensive rebuild.

Your visitors expect more

A dated, slow or confusing site costs you calls and customers, even when people do find you.

How it works

  1. 01

    We evaluate

    We use AI tools to review your site’s content, structure and performance against your competitors and how AI search sees you.

  2. 02

    We rebuild

    We update your content and structure, refresh the design, and set it up with the latest answer engine optimization (AEO) techniques. Every word is reviewed by our team, not published straight from a tool.

  3. 03

    We tighten the details

    We check your directory listings, like Google and other sites where your address and hours appear, and make sure your information is correct everywhere. We’ll also talk through cookie consent, tracking and WCAG accessibility, and add those safeguards as needed.

  4. 04

    We keep it growing

    After launch, we add fresh content written to show up in AI answers and search, and set up analytics with simple, regular reporting so you can see what’s working.

The tech specs
AI search & AEOStructured content and FAQs; schema markup (LocalBusiness, Service, FAQ and more as needed); AI crawler access settings; llms.txt.
Platform & performanceWe evaluate what’s right for your business: WordPress, Wix, a lightweight flat (static) site or another platform. Mobile-first design, Core Web Vitals tuning, XML sitemap and SSL.
ContentAI-assisted review and rewrite; every page reviewed by our team; ongoing AI-ready content after launch.
ListingsGoogle Business Profile cleanup; consistent name, address and phone across major directories.
ComplianceCookie consent and tracking setup based on the tools you use and where you do business, including Google Consent Mode v2 where it applies. WCAG accessibility review and fixes.
AnalyticsGA4 or other tools that fit your setup; conversion tracking; a simple custom dashboard showing search, AI and overall performance; regular reporting.

Final specs depend on your business, your current setup and where you operate.

FAQ

Questions about AI-ready websites.

What is AEO, and how is it different from SEO?

AEO, or answer engine optimization, is the practice of structuring your website so AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Google’s AI Overviews can understand it and cite it in their answers. SEO focuses on ranking in traditional search results. AEO focuses on being the answer. A good AI-ready website does both.

Will this help my business show up in ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini?

It improves your chances significantly. We structure your content, add schema markup and FAQs, configure AI crawler access and make sure your business information is consistent across the web. No one can guarantee placement in AI answers, but these are the signals AI tools rely on.

How much does it cost?

Every AI-ready website is scoped to your business, your competition and your budget. Pricing depends on the size of your current site and how much content needs updating. [Optional: “Most projects start at $X, plus an ongoing monthly fee for content and reporting.”]

How long does it take?

[Needs your input. For example: “Most AI-ready websites launch in 4 to 8 weeks, depending on the size of your site and how quickly we can gather information.”]

Do I have to switch website platforms?

Not necessarily. We evaluate what’s right for your business, whether that’s WordPress, Wix, a lightweight static site or another platform. If your current platform can support what you need, we’ll work with it.

Does AI write my content?

AI helps us review, organize and draft faster, which is what makes the project more affordable. Every page is reviewed and refined by our team before it goes live, so your site sounds like your business, not a chatbot.

Do I need cookie consent or accessibility updates?

It depends on the tracking tools you use and where you do business. As part of the project, we review your site and recommend what’s appropriate, from a cookie consent banner and Google Consent Mode to WCAG accessibility fixes. We add those safeguards as needed.

What happens after launch?

Your site keeps improving. We add fresh content written to show up in AI answers and search, keep your listings and schema current, and send simple, regular reports. Where it helps, that includes a custom dashboard showing search, AI and overall performance.

Is an AI-ready website right for you?

Every project is scoped to your business, your competition and your budget. Tell us about yours and we’ll come to the call with a straight answer and a few ideas.

Marketing Strategy.

Research, plan, put it to work, learn. Then do it again. A plan your team actually uses, not a report that sits on a shelf.

Marketing strategy is deciding where your time and money go, and in what order, so every channel works toward the same goals. We learn your business first, build a plan around your goals, budget and team, put it to work, and adjust as the results come in.

Straight answers

What does a marketing strategy include?

A clear picture of who buys from you and why, what you’re trying to achieve in numbers, which channels and budget will get you there, a calendar, and how you’ll know it’s working.

It should fit on a few pages your team actually reads. If a plan needs a hundred pages to explain, it’s not going to get used.

How do you choose channels on a limited budget?

Do fewer things well. Start where people are already looking for what you sell, usually search and your Google listing, then add channels as the first ones prove themselves.

We follow the money. When a channel brings in customers at a cost that works, it gets more budget. When it doesn’t, we change it or cut it.

Where does AI fit into marketing now?

In two places. The first is visibility: customers increasingly ask AI tools for recommendations, so your business needs to show up in those answers.

The second is operations. AI can take a lot of busywork off a small team, like first drafts, reporting, quoting and scheduling. We help you find where it saves real time, set it up with guardrails, and keep people reviewing the output.

How it works

  1. 01

    We learn your business first

    Your site, analytics, advertising and online presence, then conversations with your team about goals and the biggest opportunities.

  2. 02

    We set goals in numbers

    Targets you can measure, and what you can afford to spend to hit them.

  3. 03

    We plan and put it to work

    A channel plan and calendar, carried out by the same crew that built it.

  4. 04

    We learn and adjust

    Regular reviews, budget moved to what works, and the plan updated as the business changes.

What’s included
ResearchYour website, analytics, ads, listings and competitors, plus conversations with your team about goals and where the opportunities are.
Goals in numbersWhat a customer is worth, how many you need, and what you can afford to spend to get them.
Channel planWhich channels to use, in what order and with what budget, and which to skip for now.
CalendarLaunches, seasons, promotions and campaigns mapped across the year.
Measurement planWhat gets tracked, how success is judged and when we review it.
AI & automationWhere AI tools can take busywork off your team, from first drafts and reporting to quoting and scheduling.
Ongoing reviewQuarterly check-ins that adjust the plan based on what’s working.

Final scope depends on your business, your current setup and your goals.

FAQ

Questions about marketing strategy.

Can you work alongside our in-house team or other agencies?

Yes. We plug into the tools and workflows you already use and fill the gaps, whether that’s strategy, a few channels or the whole plan.

How often should a marketing plan be updated?

Set the plan once a year, review it every quarter and check the numbers monthly. If the business changes, like a new location, service or competitor, the plan changes with it.

How do you help businesses use AI?

Two ways. We help your business show up in AI search answers, and we find places where AI tools can save your team time, like drafting, reporting, quoting and scheduling. Everything is set up with guardrails and reviewed by people.

What do you need from us to get started?

Access to your analytics and ad accounts, a rough sense of your sales numbers, and a couple of conversations with the people who know your customers best. Our Let’s talk form covers most of it.

How do I choose the right digital marketing agency?

Look for a team that learns your business before recommending anything, shows real results, answers the phone, and will tell you what you don’t need. Be wary of anyone who leads with a package before asking about your goals.

Is a marketing strategy worth it for a small business?

Yes, and it doesn’t need to be big. A short plan that says what you’re doing, why and how you’ll measure it keeps a small budget from being spread too thin.

Is a marketing plan right for your business?

Businesses without a full marketing department, and marketing leads who need a partner across several channels instead of a different vendor for each.

It’s a good fit when you’re growing, adding services or locations, or spending money on marketing without a clear picture of what it’s buying.

Brand Strategy & Creative.

Practical brand work, built to be used on Monday. Not a brand book that sits in a drawer.

Brand strategy and creative is making sure your business looks, sounds and acts the same everywhere customers meet it, and that it’s clear why they should choose you. We do practical brand work your marketing can use right away: positioning and messaging, identity refreshes, brand guidelines, and the creative that carries it across your site, ads and social.

Straight answers

When does a business need a rebrand?

When your look and message no longer match who you are: you’ve grown, added services, merged, moved upmarket, or customers keep confusing you with someone else.

Most of the time the answer is a refresh, not a rebrand. Keeping what people already recognize and fixing what holds you back is faster, cheaper and less risky.

Why does brand consistency matter for search and AI?

Search engines and AI tools piece together who you are from your website, listings, reviews and social profiles. When your name, description and logo match everywhere, they’re confident they’re looking at one business.

When they don’t, your reputation gets split across what looks like several businesses, and you’re harder to recommend.

How it works

  1. 01

    We listen

    Conversations with your team and a look at how customers and competitors see you.

  2. 02

    We define

    Positioning and messaging you can say in a sentence.

  3. 03

    We design

    The identity refresh and a practical system of guidelines and templates.

  4. 04

    We roll it out

    Site, listings, social, ads and print updated together.

What’s included
Positioning & messagingWhat you do, who it’s for and why you’re the better choice, in words your whole team can repeat.
Identity refreshLogo, color and type updated to fit who you are now, keeping what customers already recognize.
Brand guidelinesA short, practical guide and ready-to-use templates, so anyone can make on-brand work.
CreativeAds, social templates, print pieces and graphics built from the system.
Consistency checkYour name, look and message lined up across your site, listings, social and signage.

Final scope depends on your business, your current setup and your goals.

FAQ

Questions about brand work.

What’s the difference between a brand refresh and a rebrand?

A refresh updates your look and message while keeping what customers already recognize. A rebrand starts over, sometimes with a new name. Most businesses need a refresh.

What’s included in brand guidelines?

Your logo and how to use it, colors, type, photo style, voice and a few real examples, plus templates for the things you make most. Short enough that people actually use it.

Do you design logos?

Yes, as part of identity work. We usually refine an existing logo rather than replace it, unless there’s a good reason to start fresh.

Will changing our brand hurt our search rankings?

Not if it’s handled carefully. Keep your business name consistent, update your website, Google profile, listings and social at the same time, and redirect any old web addresses.

Is a brand refresh right for your business?

Businesses that have outgrown their original look, added services or locations, merged with another company, or rely on many people and vendors to produce marketing materials.

Web Development.

One crew from the first sketch to launch to the Saturday-night fix. We build it, host it, keep it current and pick up the phone.

We design, build and look after websites for organizations that need more than a template: law firms with dozens of attorney profiles, banks with branch locations, health systems with provider directories, and local businesses that just need a site that works hard. Every site is fast, accessible and structured for search and AI answers.

Straight answers

Do I need a custom website, or will a template do?

It depends on what the site has to do. If you need a handful of pages and a contact form, a well-chosen template is fine, and we’ll tell you so.

Once your site needs to search 70 attorney profiles, list a dozen branches, take donations or talk to your other systems, a template starts costing more than it saves. Most of what we build sits in between: a custom design on a proven platform, made from reusable pieces your team can rearrange without calling us.

Why do website rebuilds take so long, and do they have to?

Most of the time on a website project isn’t code. It’s waiting on content, decisions and approvals. A small crew that makes decisions quickly removes most of that drag.

AI has removed a lot of the rest. We use it to audit your current site, restructure content and draft pages faster, then our team edits everything. If speed and budget matter most, our AI-ready website refresh is built for exactly that.

What happens after launch?

A website isn’t finished at launch. Plugins and platforms update, security patches land, content goes stale, and accessibility and privacy rules keep moving.

Our care plans cover updates, backups, uptime and security monitoring, and the small changes that keep a site current. Often the first you hear about a problem is our note saying it’s already fixed.

How it works

  1. 01

    We learn your business

    Your analytics, your content, the questions customers ask and what your team needs to update on its own.

  2. 02

    We plan and design

    Site map, page plan and design in your brand. You sign off on the plan before we write code.

  3. 03

    We build and test

    Development, integrations and content migration, then testing on real devices for speed and accessibility, with redirects so you keep your search value.

  4. 04

    We launch and look after it

    A watched launch, then ongoing care: updates, monitoring, fixes and improvements as you learn what works.

FAQ

Questions about web development.

What platform do you build websites on?

Most of our sites run on WordPress. We also build on Drupal, Shopify and lightweight static sites. We recommend the platform that fits what your team needs to manage and what the site has to connect to, and we’ll work with your current platform if it can do the job.

Who owns the website when it’s done?

You do. Your domain, content and accounts stay in your name, and you can take the site with you if you ever move on.

Can I update the site myself?

Yes. We set up the editor around the things you change most, like staff, events, locations and news, and train your team to use it. If you’d rather send us changes, we handle those too.

Will I lose my search rankings when you rebuild my site?

Not if the move is handled carefully. We map every old URL to its new home, set up redirects, keep the pages that already rank, and watch Search Console closely after launch to catch anything that slips.

Do you host websites?

Yes. We host on managed platforms such as WP Engine and Netlify, and our care plans include updates, backups, uptime and security monitoring.

Does my website need to be accessible?

Accessibility lawsuits and demand letters over websites have become common, and WCAG is the standard sites are measured against. Beyond the legal risk, an accessible site works better for everyone. We review your site and fix what needs fixing as part of every build.

How much does a new website cost?

It depends on how many pages, how much content needs writing and what the site has to connect to. We scope every project after an initial conversation. If budget is tight, our AI-ready website refresh is a faster, lower-cost option.

Is a new website right for your business?

Organizations whose website does real work: law firms, banks, health systems and specialty practices, associations with members, nonprofits taking donations, and local businesses ready to outgrow a do-it-yourself site.

If your site needs to connect to other systems, serve several locations or answer a lot of questions, we’re a good fit. If you need five pages by Friday, we’ll point you to our AI-ready refresh.

Tell us about yours and we’ll come to the call with a straight answer and a few ideas.

Web Hosting.

Fast, secure hosting with updates, backups and monitoring handled, and a crew that answers when something goes wrong.

We host and look after websites for businesses, health systems and nonprofits: WordPress, Drupal and static sites on managed hosting platforms built for speed and security. Updates, backups, SSL, uptime monitoring and security patches are handled, so your site stays fast and online without you having to think about it.

Straight answers

What’s the difference between managed and budget hosting?

Budget hosting rents you space on a crowded server and leaves the rest to you. Managed hosting runs on platforms tuned for WordPress, Drupal or static sites, with caching, a CDN, backups and security built in.

With us, it also comes with people: we apply updates, watch for problems and fix them, often before you notice.

Can you move our site without downtime?

Yes. We copy the site to the new host, test it on a staging address, then switch the domain over when traffic is lowest. DNS and email records come along so nothing breaks.

We handle the whole move, whether it’s one site or several.

What happens if the site goes down?

Uptime monitoring alerts us when your site stops responding, usually before your customers notice. We find the cause, fix it and tell you what happened.

There’s no ticket queue and no explaining your setup to a stranger at a help desk. You talk to the people who know your site.

How it works

  1. 01

    We review your setup

    Where you’re hosted, what’s slow or out of date, and where your email and DNS live.

  2. 02

    We pick the right home

    Managed WordPress, Drupal or static hosting matched to your traffic, platform and budget.

  3. 03

    We move it carefully

    A staging copy, testing, a planned cutover and redirects checked.

  4. 04

    We keep it running

    Updates, backups, monitoring, security and a regular check-in.

FAQ

Questions about web hosting.

Where do you host websites?

On managed platforms built for each kind of site, such as WP Engine for WordPress and Netlify for static sites. We choose based on your platform, your traffic and your budget.

Can you host a site you didn’t build?

Yes. We review it first, fix anything risky like outdated plugins, then move it and take over the upkeep.

Will moving hosts affect our email?

It shouldn’t. Email often runs separately from your website, and we copy your DNS records so mail keeps flowing during and after the move.

How often do you back up our site?

Daily, with backups kept off the server. We also take a fresh backup before every update so we can roll back if anything goes wrong.

Do you handle domain renewals?

Yes, if you’d like. We track renewal dates and DNS so your domain never lapses, and the domain stays registered in your name.

What does managed hosting cost?

It depends on the size of your site, your traffic and how much ongoing support you want. Most clients pay one monthly fee that covers hosting, updates, backups and monitoring.

Is managed hosting right for your business?

Any business or organization that wants its website fast, secure and online without managing servers, plugins and renewals itself. It matters most for healthcare and nonprofit sites, where downtime and security lapses carry real risk.

CiviCRM.

Members, donors, events and email in one system you own, connected to your website and set up the way your organization works.

CiviCRM is an open-source CRM built for nonprofits and associations. It tracks members, donors, volunteers and event registrations, takes payments and sends email, all inside your WordPress or Drupal site. We set it up, connect it to your website and payment tools, move your data in, and support it as your organization grows.

Straight answers

Is CiviCRM right for our organization?

It’s a strong fit for nonprofits, associations and member organizations that need contacts, memberships, donations and events in one place, and want to own their data without per-seat license fees. Because it’s open source, you pay for setup, hosting and support, not for every person who logs in.

If you mainly need a sales pipeline, or your team already runs on Salesforce or HubSpot, another CRM may serve you better, and we’ll tell you so.

How does it work with our website?

CiviCRM runs inside your WordPress or Drupal site, so membership signups, donation forms and event registrations live on your own pages and go straight into your records. No more exporting spreadsheets between systems.

We match the forms to your site’s design and set up the payment processor, confirmation emails and receipts.

What happens to our existing data?

We map what you have, whether it’s spreadsheets, an old CRM or an email platform, clean up duplicates and import it, so past gifts, membership terms and event attendance come with you.

Then we train your staff on the day-to-day work, so the system gets used.

How it works

Straight answers

Shopify, Amazon or both?

Your own store gives you your brand, your margins and your customer list. Amazon and Walmart give you shoppers who are already there, in exchange for fees, strict rules and a marketplace that keeps the customer relationship.

Most growing brands need both, with the store as home base and marketplaces for reach. We set them up to work together: the same product information everywhere, and inventory kept in sync so you don’t sell what you don’t have.

What makes an online store actually sell?

Great product photos, clear options, fast pages and a short checkout. Then the part most stores skip: answering the questions shoppers ask before they buy, like sizing, materials, care, shipping and returns, right on the product page.

Those same answers are what AI shopping tools and search results pull from. A product page that answers questions sells better to people and gets recommended more by machines.

Why does it help to have one team on all of it?

Launching a new collection touches everything at once: the photo shoot, the store, the marketplace listings, the ads, the emails and the stock on the shelf. When each piece sits with a different vendor, every launch turns into a relay race and something gets dropped.

With one crew, it’s one plan and one calendar. We’ve run model shoots, built the listings, launched the ads and packed the orders for the same brand in the same week.

AI Search Visibility.

Rank in search. Get named in AI answers. And know whether it’s working, because we check what the AI tools actually say about you.

AI search visibility is the work of getting your business understood, trusted and cited by AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity and Google’s AI Overviews. It builds on traditional SEO and adds the structure answer engines rely on. You’ll also hear it called AEO (answer engine optimization) or GEO (generative engine optimization).

Straight answers

What’s the difference between SEO, AEO and GEO?

SEO gets you ranked in the list of search results. AEO gets you chosen as the direct answer, whether that’s a featured snippet, a voice assistant reply or an AI Overview. GEO gets you cited when a generative AI tool writes its own answer.

In practice they overlap so much that we treat them as one job. The same clear pages, accurate facts and solid technical setup serve all three. The acronyms matter less than whether you show up when a customer asks.

How do AI tools decide what to cite?

No AI company publishes the formula, but the patterns are consistent. AI tools favor pages that answer the question clearly near the top, that agree with what other trusted sources say, and that come from businesses with a visible track record: reviews, listings, mentions and a site that’s been around.

Many of these tools also run a live web search behind the scenes before they answer. That’s why traditional SEO still matters. If search engines can’t find and understand your pages, AI tools usually can’t either.

Is SEO dead?

No. It’s the plumbing everything else runs on. What’s changing is the click. Simple questions now often get answered right on the results page or in a chat window, so some of those visits never reach your site.

The visits that do come tend to be further along: they’ve already read the answer and want to talk to someone. So we measure differently, too. Mentions in AI answers, AI referral traffic, calls and form fills tell you more than raw traffic does now.

How it works

  1. 01

    We measure where you stand

    A visibility baseline across the major AI tools, plus an SEO and technical audit of your site against your top competitors.

  2. 02

    We fix the foundation

    Indexing, speed, crawler settings, schema and listings: the things that decide whether machines can read and trust you.

  3. 03

    We write for the questions

    Your most important pages rewritten to answer first, and new pages for the questions you’re missing. AI helps us draft; our team edits every word.

  4. 04

    We check and repeat

    We rerun the baseline on a schedule, report what changed and adjust. It’s ongoing work, because the tools keep changing.

What’s included

Question researchThe real questions people ask before they buy, pulled from your sales and service team, search data, site search and reviews.

FAQ

Questions about AI search.

How do you measure AI search visibility?

We ask the AI tools the questions your customers ask and record whether you’re named, how you’re described and who shows up instead. We repeat the same set of questions on a schedule, and pair it with Google Search Console and AI referral traffic in GA4, so you can see the trend rather than a single snapshot.

How long does it take to show up in AI answers?

Technical fixes and schema can be in place within weeks. How fast AI tools reflect them varies: tools that search the web live can pick up changes quickly, while answers drawn from a model’s training data update far less often. Plan on months, not days, and measure the trend.

Should I block AI crawlers from my website?

For most businesses that want to be recommended, no. Blocking AI crawlers can keep you out of the answers you’re trying to appear in. Some AI companies run separate crawlers for training and for live search, so you can allow one and block the other. We’ll walk through the tradeoffs and set it up to match your goals.

What is llms.txt, and do I need one?

llms.txt is a proposed plain-text file that points AI tools to your most important pages. It isn’t an official standard, and major AI tools haven’t confirmed they rely on it. It’s quick and cheap to add, so we include it, but it ranks well below clear content, schema and solid SEO.

Does schema markup help with AI answers?

It helps machines read your key facts without guessing: who you are, what you offer, where you work and what your FAQs say. Google uses it for rich results, and it removes ambiguity for every other system that reads your site. It isn’t a switch that guarantees a mention, but it’s part of the foundation.

Do I need to rewrite my whole website?

No. We start with the pages that answer the questions that bring you business: your services, FAQs, comparisons and how you work. Rewriting those to answer first and adding the questions you’re missing usually matters more than touching every page.

Will AI-assisted content hurt my rankings?

Google has said it rewards helpful content however it’s produced, and goes after low-quality content mass-produced to game rankings. We use AI to research and draft faster, and every page is reviewed and edited by our team before it goes live.

Do I need to care about Bing?

Yes, a little. Bing’s index powers Microsoft Copilot and has been one of the sources behind other AI tools. Setting up Bing Webmaster Tools and submitting your sitemap is free and takes minutes, so we do it as part of the foundation.

Is AI search visibility right for your business?

Any business whose customers research before they reach out: health systems and specialty practices, law firms and professional services, manufacturers and B2B companies, nonprofits, and online stores selling considered purchases.

And anyone who has asked ChatGPT for a recommendation in their own field and heard a competitor’s name instead of their own.

Local SEO & Reputation.

Accurate listings everywhere. A Google profile that does the selling. Reviews coming in steadily, with every one answered. And reporting that counts calls, not just clicks.

Local SEO gets your business found when someone nearby searches for what you do: on Google Maps, in search results and, more and more, in AI answers. Reputation is what makes them call once they find you. We handle both, from your Google Business Profile and directory listings to the reviews and pages that back them up.

Straight answers

How does Google decide who shows up nearby?

Google says local results come down to three things: relevance, distance and prominence. Relevance is how well your business matches the search. Distance is how close you are to the person searching. Prominence is how well known and well regarded you are, which is where reviews, listings and your website come in.

You can’t move your shop closer to every customer. You can make sure Google has complete, accurate information about what you do, and that the rest of the web agrees with it. That’s most of the job, and it’s the part most businesses never finish.

Why does it matter more now that AI answers questions?

Ask ChatGPT, Gemini or Google’s AI Overviews for a good landscaper or a pediatric dentist nearby, and they put together an answer from many of the same places Google Maps uses: your business profile, directory listings, reviews and your own website.

When those sources agree, you’re easy to recommend. When your hours are wrong on one site and your old address is still on another, you’re easy to leave out. The cleanup that helps you on the map is the same cleanup that helps you in AI answers.

What makes a review strategy work?

Timing and follow-through. The best moment to ask is right after a job goes well, while the customer still feels good about it. Make it one tap: a short link in a text or email, or a QR code on the invoice. Then reply to every review, especially the bad ones. Future customers read your replies as closely as the reviews.

We never write, buy or filter reviews. Asking only the customers you think are happy breaks Google’s rules, and so do paid or fake reviews. Real reviews, asked for consistently, win over time.

How it works

  1. 01

    We search like your customers

    We look you up in Google, Maps and AI tools from the neighborhoods you serve, then audit your profile, listings, reviews and top competitors.

  2. 02

    We fix the foundation

    Profile cleanup, corrected and merged listings, LocalBusiness schema, and service and location pages that back it all up.

  3. 03

    We get reviews moving

    A simple ask built into how you already close out jobs, plus monitoring and a reply to every review.

  4. 04

    We keep it current

    Monthly posts and photos, listing checks when hours or services change, and a short report on calls and trends.

FAQ

Questions about local SEO.

How long does local SEO take to work?

Fixes to your Google Business Profile and listings often show up within a few weeks. Rankings, review volume and steady calls build over several months, and businesses that keep at it month to month pull ahead of the ones that stop after a cleanup.

Do I need a storefront to show up in local search?

No. Service-area businesses like plumbers, landscapers and mobile services can hide their street address on Google and list the areas they serve instead. You still need a real, verifiable business.

What does NAP consistency mean, and why does it matter?

NAP is your business name, address and phone number. Search engines and AI tools compare it across your Google profile, your website and directories. Mismatches, like an old suite number or a different phone number on Yelp, make your listing harder to trust and easier to leave out.

Can you remove bad reviews?

Only Google can remove a review, and only if it breaks Google’s rules, such as spam, fake engagement or offensive content. We flag those. For honest negative reviews, a calm, specific reply does more for you than removal would. Future customers read how you respond.

Do you write or buy reviews?

No. Fake or paid reviews break Google’s policies and federal rules, and they put your listing at risk. We help you ask real customers at the right moment and make it easy for them to say yes.

Do you work with businesses that have multiple locations?

Yes. For multi-location businesses and health systems we manage location pages, provider directories and listings across every site, so hours, addresses and phone numbers stay accurate everywhere at once.

How is local SEO different from AI search visibility?

Local SEO focuses on nearby searches: the map results and “near me” questions. AI search visibility covers how AI tools understand and cite your business more broadly. They share a foundation, and most local businesses need both.

How much does local SEO cost?

It depends on how many locations you have and how much cleanup your listings need. Most clients start with a one-time cleanup, then move to monthly support for reviews, updates and reporting. We scope it after an initial conversation.

Is local SEO right for your business?

Any business whose customers find it by searching nearby: contractors and trades, landscapers, restaurants, retailers, medical and dental offices, law firms and community banks.

It scales up, too. For multi-location health systems we manage provider directories and location pages across many sites, and we handle after-hours and emergency updates when something can’t wait until Monday.

Straight answers

Where should my ad budget go?

Start where the intent is. Search ads reach people who are already looking for what you sell, so they usually come first. Social, streaming TV and display build demand with people who aren’t looking yet, and retargeting brings back the ones who almost bought.

The mix depends on the business. A local service company leans on search and local ads. An online store leans on shopping, marketplace and social. A B2B firm might pair search with LinkedIn. We always hold back part of the budget to test, then move money to what works.

How do you know if ads are working?

Not by clicks. We set up tracking for the things that matter, like calls, forms, bookings and sales, before the first ad runs, then report cost per result in plain English.

Where it makes sense, we connect results from your CRM or store back to the ad platforms, so they learn to find more customers, not more clickers.

What’s changing now that AI runs the ad platforms?

Google and Meta now automate most of the bidding and targeting. That automation works well with good inputs, like accurate conversion tracking, strong creative and clear goals, and wastes money quickly with bad ones.

Our job has shifted with it: feed the platforms clean data and good creative, set the guardrails, and watch closely. No autopilot campaigns.

Content Marketing.

Your experts talk on a short call. We turn it into pages search engines and AI tools want to quote.

Content marketing is publishing useful, expert answers that bring customers to you: in search, in AI answers and in their inbox. We build it from your team’s real expertise, using short interviews with your subject-matter experts and turning them into pages written to be found and cited.

Straight answers

What kind of content gets cited by AI tools?

Specific, expert, first-hand answers. Generic posts written from other generic posts are everywhere now, and AI tools have little reason to quote them.

What they can’t find anywhere else is your experience: the way your team explains a procedure, prices a job or solves a problem. That’s the content we build.

Why interviews instead of asking our team to write?

Your experts don’t have time to write, and most would rather talk anyway. A short call captures the real details and the way they actually explain things.

How much time does this take from our experts?

Email Marketing.

The channel you own. Written in your voice, sent on a plan, measured in sales and sign-ups.

We plan, design and send email and text marketing that brings customers back: newsletters, welcome series, abandoned-cart and seasonal campaigns, and member and donor communications. Every campaign is built for your list, tested before it goes out, and measured by what it brings in.

Straight answers

Is email marketing still worth it?

Yes. It’s the one channel you own outright. No algorithm decides whether your customers see it, and the list goes with you if you change platforms.

For online stores, associations and nonprofits especially, email is often the most reliable source of repeat sales, renewals and donations.

Why are my emails going to spam?

Usually it’s setup or list health. Gmail and Yahoo tightened their rules for bulk senders in 2024, and senders without proper authentication (SPF, DKIM and DMARC) or with old, unengaged lists are the first to get filtered.

We fix the technical setup, clean the list and keep a steady sending rhythm, which together do more for deliverability than any subject line trick.

    The calendar, the content and the flows that run on their own.

  4. 04

    We send, test and report

    Test sends, live monitoring and a monthly report on results.

FAQ

Questions about email marketing.

How often should I email my list?

Often enough to stay familiar, rarely enough that every email is worth opening. For most businesses that’s somewhere between twice a month and once a week, plus automated emails triggered by what people do.

Which email platform should I use?

Usually the one you already have, if it can do what you need. If not, we’ll recommend a platform that fits your size, your store or CRM and your budget, and move your list over.

Can you add text message marketing?

Yes. We set up SMS campaigns and alerts with clear opt-in language, consent records and easy opt-out, since text marketing carries stricter consent rules than email.

How do I grow my email list?

Give people a reason to join: a useful guide, early access, a first-order offer or event updates. Then ask in the right places, like your site, checkout, events and social, and never buy a list.

What email results should I track?

Open and click rates tell you whether people are interested. Sales, registrations, donations and unsubscribes tell you whether it’s working. We report both.

Is email marketing right for your business?

Online stores that want repeat buyers, associations communicating with members, nonprofits keeping donors close, and service businesses with a list they’ve never really used.

What kind of video should my business make first?

Analytics, Attribution & Reporting.

One set of numbers you can trust, one dashboard you’ll actually open, and a person who explains what changed.

Analytics is how you know what your marketing is actually doing. We set up tracking for the things that matter, like calls, forms, bookings and sales, make it respect your visitors’ privacy choices, and bring it together in one dashboard and a short, plain-English report.

Straight answers

Why don’t my numbers match across tools?

GA4, Google Ads, Meta and your CRM will never agree exactly. Each counts differently, each ad platform gives itself credit, and visitors who decline cookies or use ad blockers show up in some tools and not others.

The fix isn’t forcing them to match. It’s agreeing on which source answers which question, for example, your CRM for revenue and GA4 for site behavior, and knowing why the others differ.

What should I actually be measuring?

The things that pay the bills: calls, form fills, bookings, sales, and what each one costs you. Then a few early signals that predict them, like search visibility, mentions in AI answers and returning visitors.

Page views, followers and impressions are fine to glance at. They shouldn’t drive decisions on their own.

How do privacy rules change tracking?

More visitors now choose what they’ll allow, and the rules differ by where they live. A consent banner and Google Consent Mode let you respect those choices and still measure in aggregate.

Healthcare organizations face extra scrutiny over what tracking tools collect, especially on pages about appointments, conditions or patient portals. We set those sites up so third-party tools don’t receive information they shouldn’t.

How it works

  1. 01

    We audit what’s tracked

    What’s installed, what’s firing, what’s missing and what’s double-counting.

  2. 02

    We fix the plumbing

    Tags, events, conversions, call tracking and consent, set up cleanly and documented.

  3. 03

    We build the dashboard

    One view of search, AI, ads and leads, built around the questions you ask most.

  4. 04

    We review it with you

    A short monthly report and a regular conversation about what to do next.

FAQ

Questions about analytics.

What is GA4, and do I still need it?

GA4 is the current version of Google Analytics, and it’s free. Most websites should have it set up properly, sometimes alongside other tools for calls, ecommerce or privacy-focused tracking.

What is Google Consent Mode?

Consent Mode tells Google’s tags how to behave based on what each visitor agreed to on your cookie banner. Google requires it for advertisers reaching visitors in the European Economic Area, and it’s good practice anywhere you use a consent banner.

Can healthcare websites use analytics safely?

Yes, with care. Healthcare sites need to control what tracking tools collect, especially on pages tied to appointments, conditions or patient portals. We configure analytics so third parties don’t receive protected health information, recommend privacy-focused tools where needed, and work with your compliance team to sign off on the setup.

How can I see traffic from ChatGPT and other AI tools?

Visits from many AI tools show up in GA4 as referrals from sites like chatgpt.com and perplexity.ai. We group them into their own channel so you can track the trend. Not every AI visit passes along where it came from, so the real number is usually higher.

What is attribution?

Attribution is how credit for a sale or lead is split across the ads, searches and visits that came before it. GA4 uses a data-driven model by default. We look at it alongside simpler views, like last click and first visit, so decisions don’t hinge on one model’s opinion.

Can you fix analytics someone else set up?

Yes. We audit what’s there, keep what works, fix what’s broken and document it, so the next person isn’t starting from scratch.

Is better reporting right for your business?

Any business spending money on marketing that can’t say with confidence what’s working. That includes businesses whose analytics was set up years ago by someone who has since moved on.

It’s especially important for healthcare organizations and multi-location businesses, where privacy rules and scale make tracking easy to get wrong.
